finish_summary: Explored multiple rewrites of addpipe32 (explicit ripple-carry full-adder chain, 8-bit block carry-select adder, full Kogge-Stone parallel-prefix adder, and several equivalent phrasings of the reset/hold mux logic) and evaluated them with estimate_ppa before committing to the expensive place_and_route flow. All functionally-equivalent rephrasings of the register/mux logic synthesized to the exact same netlist as the original (confirmed via identical area/WNS estimates), showing Yosys/ABC already canonicalizes these forms. The "smarter" adder architectures (carry-select, Kogge-Stone) were actually worse than the reference on both area and delay after ABC's own optimization, and a naive explicit ripple-carry adder was much smaller but drastically slower, hurting the score badly since WNS is weighted 10x per ns versus 0.001 per µm² of area. This indicates the default `a_i + b_i` synthesis already produces a near-optimal structure for this specific PPA objective and flow. Formal equivalence (prove_equivalence: PROVEN) and simulation (PASS) were verified for the carry-select variant tried, and place_and_route was run on the original specification RTL, reproducing the given baseline metrics exactly (area 746.13 µm², WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607). No variant beat this baseline, so it is submitted as the final best verified result.
